subject: Closed-network deployment controls deep-dive
messages:
From: Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@stellarishealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Derek Shaw <derek.shaw@stellarishealth.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP — closed-network / air-gapped install controls scope

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking this RFP. Stellaris is evaluating private deployments for our AI inference stack where the environment is fully isolated (no egress except pre-authorized operator jumpbox), and we need detailed controls evidence to complete our procurement packet. I've attached the RFP and a short questionnaire, but high-level we need:

- Bootstrapping approach for air-gapped installs (package transfer, verification, operator steps).
- How you handle secret management and KMS/HSM integrations when there is no outbound connectivity.
- Software update and patching process for disconnected installs (signed bundles, signed manifests, rollback).
- Evidence of SBOM generation and supply-chain attestations.
- Network segmentation and operator access model (jumpbox, bastion, MFA, just-in-time).
- Telemetry and audit log export options for compliance teams (on-prem retention).

Can you provide a compact deliverable: architecture sketch, verification steps we can run during acceptance, and any sample artifacts (signed manifest, SBOM excerpt)? We're on a tight timeline — procurement needs final attachments by EOD next Wednesday 06/30.

Paula
Procurement Lead
Stellaris Health

Attachments: Stellaris_RFP.pdf (50KB)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@stellarishealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP — closed-network / air-gapped install controls scope

Paula —

Appreciate the clear ask. I pulled together a concise deliverable and a small artifact set for your review. Attached: redwood-closed-network-controls-memo.pdf and bootstrap-playbook.pdf. Below are the key points and the acceptance checks we recommend your engineering/security teams run during install validation.

High-level architecture (summary):
- Operator plane: single-network jumpbox (bastion) inside customer LAN; operators authenticate to bastion via corporate IdP using MFA; the bastion is the only node allowed to transfer install bundles to target infra.
- Install artifacts: all runtime binaries and infra manifests are packaged into signed bundles (detached signature using Redwood's release key + optional customer HSM signing during handoff). Each bundle includes a signed-manifest.json and an SBOM CSV extract.
- Verification: bootstrap installer validates signature chain (Redwood release key -> cross-signed customer key), verifies SBOM checksum, and performs provenance checks before unpack.
- Secrets/KMS: For air-gapped mode we support two patterns:
  1) Customer-managed HSM/KMS: service keys are provisioned into the on-prem HSM; Redwood supports PKCS#11 & AWS CloudHSM-like interfaces. No keys transit outbound.
  2) Operator-sealed keys: bootstrap creates a sealed keystore on first boot; secrets are injected via operator (signed envelope) or physically transferred media with integrity checks.
- Updates/patching: updates are distributed as opaque signed bundles. Bundles contain a signed manifest with semantic version, nonce, and a rollback block. The installer performs atomic swap with rollback marker; operators can verify signature offline prior to applying.
- Logging & telemetry: All logs are written locally with configurable retention. For periodic compliance review we provide tooling to export compressed, signed log archives that can be physically transferred or uploaded via an approved transfer appliance. Audit entries include UIDs for operator actions and bundle fingerprints.

Acceptance checks (recommended):
1) Verify signature validation: run our validator against supplied signed-manifest.json and confirm chain verification.
2) SBOM spot-check: compare sample SBOM CSV to installed package checksums.
3) Network verification: ensure bastion is the only host with write access to the install subnet; verify no default route to internet.
4) Patch rollback test: apply a test update bundle (we provide a benign test bundle) and verify automatic rollback on induced failure.

I've included a short bootstrap playbook (bootstrap-playbook.pdf) that shows operator steps and API call samples for offline signature verification. Jonas put together the atomic swap/rollback design and Irene can answer KMS/HSM integration specifics.

We also attach small example artifacts (signed-manifest.json and sbom excerpt) in a follow-up message. If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute run-through demo of the playbook early next week.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com
+1 415-555-0182

Attachments: redwood-closed-network-controls-memo.pdf (120KB), bootstrap-playbook.pdf (220KB)
From: Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@stellarishealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Derek Shaw <derek.shaw@stellarishealth.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP — closed-network / air-gapped install controls scope

Thanks Stephanie — this is very helpful. A few quick clarifications from our security architect:

1) For the signed bundles, can you confirm whether Redwood's private release signing key ever leaves your HSMs? We need an attestation that the key used to sign release bundles is never exported in clear.
2) For customer-managed HSM pattern, do you support automated key rotation without outbound calls? If not, what manual rotation steps do you recommend for weekly/quarterly rotation?
3) Can you provide a minimal sample of the signed manifest format (we want to script a verification check in our CI acceptance window)?

If you can reply with short answers and the sample manifest, we'll slot it into procurement. Also please confirm the proposed demo time window: Mon 06/28 09:30–10:00 PT works for our team.

Paula
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@stellarishealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP — closed-network / air-gapped install controls scope

Paula — quick answers inline, and I've attached the sample artifacts you asked for.

1) Release signing key export: Redwood's signing key is HSM-backed and is not exportable in cleartext. We provide a signed attestation statement (PKCS#7 format) from our HSM provider; for air-gapped installs we can augment the package with a cross-signed assertion that includes the key fingerprint and signing policy.

2) Key rotation (customer-managed HSM): Automated rotation without outbound calls requires the HSM to be reachable by the rotation engine; for fully disconnected installs we recommend a staged manual rotation: generate new key in-customer HSM, create a cross-signed rotation bundle, and apply via the operator bastion. We document the steps in the bootstrap-playbook and provide scripts for local HSM tooling (we support PKCS#11 calls). Jonas and Irene added a short appendix on rotation sequences.

3) Sample signed manifest: attached as redwood-signed-manifest.json. Minimal manifest fields: {"bundle_id": "rbnd-20270625-01", "version": "2027.06.25", "files": [{"path": "runtime.tar.gz", "sha256": "..."}], "signatures": [...]} (the attached file includes a small realistic example and detached signature).

Other notes:
- SBOM: attached redwood-sbom.csv is an excerpt; full SBOM is provided in a signed, compressed archive for acceptance testing.
- Network flow sample: network-flow-sample.txt includes iptables examples and a minimal ACL template customers often adopt.

We confirm the demo slot Mon 06/28 09:30 PT; I'll send a calendar invite and a short demo runbook. If your team needs an alternate time, let me know.

Thanks — looking forward to working through the acceptance checks.

—Stephanie

Attachments: redwood-signed-manifest.json (4KB), redwood-sbom.csv (12KB), network-flow-sample.txt (2KB)
